scorecard.key_number: cost cap spends 102.4% of its budget; Lead gen | FY26 Q4 at 107.2% of expected spend
scorecard.why: The cost cap isn't too tight, and the lead gen group is on pace. Maximum delivery on the expansion-on lead gen campaign costs 1.55 times the cost-cap campaign per lead, a reason to test a cap there. Every flight is 14 days or longer.

Conversation ad | Ops directors | Demo invite has nothing to rotate in. proposed_structure: Keep Lead gen | FY26 Q4 for lead gen, with its total budget and end date, and Demo | Always on for demos; give the demo group a total budget too, so it can be paced.

Inside the demo group, one prospecting campaign per audience you want to judge apart: split the two demo campaigns by sector (for example clinics and gyms on one, salons and spas on the other), so each has its own pool and cost per demo.
Keep retargeting in its own campaign and exclude its site-visitor audience from the prospecting campaigns, so the same person isn't bought twice.
2 to 5 ads per campaign: add a second conversation ad variant so the message campaign has something to compare.
Live on the same dates for at least 14 days before comparing campaigns.
